items.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: He paid his musical dues in New York City and found work with jazz greats Red Norvo, Miff Mole and Bunny Berigan.

ctx.x: Trumpeter Jack Palmer has seen it all in the music business. A native of Rome, New York, he was initiated into entertainment in the thriving music scene at Sylvan Beach, New York in the mid-1930s. He paid his musical dues in New York City and found work with jazz greats Red Norvo, Miff Mole and Bunny Berigan. Jack was an important port of the Harry James Orchestra and roommate of an up-and-coming singer named Frank Sinatra. He performed on television and records with The Jackie Gleason Orchestra and his…
Jack was interviewed at Hamilton College on September 24, 1997 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive. Jack’s son, drummer Jack Palmer Jr., was also present during the interview.
